title: 0.7.0 pre-tag checklist and release gate
description:
The durable home for lore-cli's 0.7.0 pre-tag checklist. It exists because on 2026-09-14 that list
lived ONLY in cross-session messages to an orchestrator that was about to be cleared -- which is not
a record, it is a conversation. Anything that fires ON a tag, or that is cheaper to fix before one
than after, belongs here as it is found.

0.7.0 is a PAIR release with quest 0.7.0. The two version numbers move in lockstep from 0.5.0 and
must match before either tags. Campaign is OPAG-142 on opum-agent.

=== THE GATE, per the user via opum-agent, 2026-09-14 ===

Nothing publishes until the backlogs are complete AND all E2E testing is done. opum-cli-e2e is
building a true project-based E2E test at the level a real integration consumer drives the products
(their TASK-62, a Quest-backed project-lifecycle suite), and the pair does not ship until that
qualifies it. The feature burndown is the long pole, not the publish mechanics.

PUBLISH ROUTE IS SETTLED AND IS NOT A BLOCKER: 0.7.0 publishes MANUALLY, same as 0.6.2. LCLI-482
(OIDC trusted publishing broken by GitHub immutable subject claims) is explicitly NOT a release
blocker for 0.7.0 -- it and OPAG-127 stay open for the release AFTER this one, coordinated by the
orchestrator. Do not plan around it and do not attempt the fix as part of this release.

=== CHECKLIST ===

1. LCLI-494 -- FIX IT BEFORE THE TAG, NOT AFTER. This is the item with a real deadline rather than a
   preference. Projection schema 1.1 is on main but NOT YET PUBLISHED, so correcting
   `sourceAdapterVersion` (which claims "backlog-json/1" on Quest-backed exports) now makes the
   correction part of 1.1's definition and no consumer ever sees the intermediate state. After the
   tag, 1.1 has shipped with the field lying and the fix needs its own 1.2 plus a compatibility
   story for records 0.7.0 itself emitted. Same work, materially cheaper before. See LCLI-494's own
   sizing note.

2. LCLI-469 -- notify opum-marketplace of the new tag so it re-resolves the federated skills/ SHA.
   FIRES ON THE TAG. Decide it before tagging, not after.

3. THE NPM TOKEN. It was exposed in a transcript on 2026-09-14 and the user deferred rotation to
   "the next release window" -- 0.7.0 IS that window, and the manual publish path uses it. NOT a
   lore-cli decision: this is the user's, directly. It belongs on this list so it is remembered
   before the publish rather than discovered during it.

4. VERSION BUMP ACROSS THE FAMILY -- package.json plus the six npm/<platform>/package.json manifests,
   and CHANGELOG's `## [Unreleased]` promoted to `## [0.7.0] - <date>`.

5. THE PROVENANCE WARNING MUST BE REPEATED. 0.6.2's changelog entry explains that it ships with NO
   provenance attestation because a manual publish cannot mint one. 0.7.0 publishes manually too, so
   its entry needs the same warning. Do not let the absence read as tampering.

6. RE-ASK QUEST-CLI FOR PRE-TAG ITEMS IMMEDIATELY BEFORE TAGGING, not once during planning
   (quest-cli's own suggestion, 2026-09-14). They had nothing in the "wrong today, expensive after
   0.7.0 ships" category at the time of asking, but QCLI-284/287 were still landing and could
   surface something. The window closes for both repos at the same moment.

7. THE PROSE-DETECTION GAP, carried from LCLI-479. Nothing in this repo verifies that a command named
   in documentation actually exists -- which is how `lore manifest --json` reached a shipped changelog
   entry and LCLI-479's own acceptance criteria past three reviews (there is no such command; it is
   `lore help --json`). test/help.test.ts's manifest/router lockstep guard covers only the opposite
   direction: every manifest command dispatches. A docs-name-a-real-command check is small and would
   have caught it. Not a tag blocker -- listed so it is a decision rather than an omission.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY DONE FOR 0.7.0 ===

LCLI-479 (required flags in help and the machine manifest), LCLI-476 (dependency edges reach
projections/traversal/export, schema 1.1), LCLI-492 (lore sync --fail-on-drop). All on main at
44303b8f.

STILL OPEN IN THE FEATURE BURNDOWN: LCLI-477 (typed authored relationships -- deliberately unstarted,
it is the most design-shaped of the five and should be begun fresh), LCLI-478 (hard maxTokens budget
plus exact-read; BLOCKED on the shared shape with quest's QCLI-276 -- quest has recorded their half as
DEC-3 and lore owes a matching record). Also open: LCLI-494, LCLI-495, LCLI-491 (Ladybug flake).

=== THE RELEASE'S OWN FRAMING, agreed with quest-cli and adopted by opum-agent ===

"0.7.0 makes the graph and the contract legible to an agent, not just to a reader."
Shared principle: "anything an agent parses must be able to express what it does not currently say."
And the line worth using in the notes: we found the defect in ourselves in the same week we named it
-- LCLI-476 alone turned up two hard-coded version literals where a constant belonged, neither
tested, one of which announced a schema version it did not emit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: LCLI-494 is resolved BEFORE the tag, or a deliberate decision is recorded here to let it ship wrong and correct it in 1.2 — not left to be discovered after tagging.
LCLI-469 is decided before the tag, since it fires ON the tag (opum-marketplace re-resolves the federated skills/ SHA).
The npm token question is put to the USER directly before the publish — not to the orchestrator, and not discovered during it.
Version numbers match quest 0.7.0 exactly, bumped across package.json and all six npm/<platform> manifests, with CHANGELOG [Unreleased] promoted to [0.7.0] and dated.
0.7.0`s changelog entry repeats the no-provenance-attestation warning, since it publishes manually like 0.6.2 and an absent attestation must not read as tampering.
quest-cli is re-asked for pre-tag items immediately before tagging, not only during planning.
The release gate is satisfied: the feature backlog is complete AND opum-cli-e2e`s project-based E2E qualification has passed against the pair.

=== THREE CORRECTIONS TO A STALE BRIEF, verified against live state ===

The recycled orchestrator's handoff brief cited three facts that are no longer true. Recorded here rather than only in message traffic, because the next reader may be handed the same stale brief.

1. "dev is +6 vs main and unpromoted" -- NO. dev was promoted and main is identical to it.

3. "close or annotate any In Progress task" -- there are none. `quest task list --status "In Progress"` is empty, and the working tree is clean.

THE ONE PREMISE THAT WAS CORRECT is LCLI-491, and it is carried below unchanged.

=== STANDING INSTRUCTIONS, recorded as asked ===

LCLI-491 -- DO NOT RAISE THE LADYBUG TIMEOUT before the real distribution is measured. The projection-lifecycle test times out at 5000ms intermittently; raising the bound without measuring how long it actually takes converts a flake into a slower flake and destroys the evidence needed to fix it. Untouched by this campaign and to stay that way.

LCLI-498 AND LCLI-499 ARE SEPARATE ON PURPOSE, and both records already say so from their own side -- so a reader arriving at either finds the reasoning without needing the other. 499's summary: "Warn on every fallback" and "report the backend on every response" are different fixes; only the second was ruled in. 498's summary: making the previously-silent fallback route warn belongs WITH the naming-the-cause work, because "the advisory names its cause" and "the advisory is emitted" are one defect from two angles, and shipping the first alone gives a warning that names its cause except when there is none. opum-agent left that call to this repository and confirmed it afterwards.

=== WHAT THE 0.7.0 GATE STILL NEEDS, none of it lore implementation ===

Checklist items 2-7 on this task, unchanged: LCLI-469 (fires ON the tag), the npm token question which goes to the USER directly, the version bump across package.json and the six npm/<platform> manifests with CHANGELOG [Unreleased] -> [0.7.0] dated to match quest 0.7.0 exactly, the no-provenance-attestation warning repeated, and quest-cli re-asked for pre-tag items immediately before tagging.

AND THE UNRESOLVED SEQUENCING PROBLEM, which is a decision and not a task: the user's instruction is that nothing publishes until the backlogs are complete AND all E2E testing is done, but opum-cli-e2e's qualification resolves both packages from npm at 0.7.0 -- so it cannot run before the publish it is meant to gate. The instruction as given has no satisfiable ordering. opum-agent took it to the user rather than ruling, which is right: the step it collides on is the one they reserved. Do not pick an ordering silently.

The two shapes, so whoever picks this up does not re-derive them: qualifying pre-publish means qualifying against something other than the published artifact, which weakens it to roughly what CI already proves; publishing first means the gate becomes a rollback trigger rather than a gate. Different guarantees, neither obviously right -- it turns on whether "all E2E testing done" means "before anyone can install it" or "before we tell anyone to".

The relay was accurate in every particular. Checking it anyway cost one command and is the only

AC 6 -- QUEST-CLI RE-ASKED IMMEDIATELY BEFORE TAGGING, and the answer was NOT "nothing". Their
finding: 0.7.0's `contractVersion` entry says what the field covers and never what it does not,
while 0.7.0 ships two consumer-visible changes it does not cover (the pause status rename to
"Paused", and error envelopes carrying no contractVersion at all). CHANGELOG-only fix, cheap before
the tag and an erratum after, because the CHANGELOG ships INSIDE the npm tarball and is frozen there.

ASKING THEM IS WHAT FOUND LORE'S OWN COPY OF IT, which is the entire argument for item 6 existing
and is worth recording as the justification rather than the anecdote. Verified empirically against
the 0.7.0 binary, not read off source:

  lore context <id> --json                   -> target.body PRESENT, schemaVersion 1, no `omitted`
  lore context <id> --max-tokens 60 --json   -> target.body ABSENT,  schemaVersion 1,
                                                omitted.fields ["target.body"]

--max-tokens existed in 0.6.2 and ALWAYS emitted the body -- an oversized target went out in full,
merely flagged `truncated`. So for a caller supplying a budget, a field that was always present can
now be absent while the only version signal does not move. cli-contract section 7.1 lists
"renaming, REMOVING, or repurposing an existing field" as requiring a schemaVersion bump.

THE CLAIM IS NOT THAT LORE SHIPS A 7.1 VIOLATION, and the distinction is the point. There is a real
argument it is not one: the old behavior was a documented defect, and data.omitted.fields names
every removed field and is present even when empty, which is the correct application of the
principle. The defect was that this is a JUDGEMENT and the release never recorded it -- a 0.6.2
consumer reading target.body on a budgeted call gets undefined on 0.7.0 and every signal they can
read says nothing changed. Fixed in this PR by one CHANGELOG bullet that adjudicates it against 7.1
and states the reasoning, not only the verdict.

=== A PAIR-LEVEL FACT NEITHER REPO COULD SEE ALONE ===

opum-cli-e2e's strict error-envelope allow-list lives in the SHARED lib/check.mjs (lines 181-183),

So "there is no cheap moment to add envelope metadata to error envelopes later" is not a quest-cli
fact. It binds BOTH CLIs, permanently, until opum-cli-e2e changes first. This is why neither repo
should treat the missing metadata on its error envelopes as an oversight to fix in a later release:
the fix turns their checks red whenever it lands. opum-agent routed it to opum-cli-e2e as a standing
constraint so the next session in either repo does not rediscover it at the same cost.

=== THE release.yml ASYMMETRY, accepted rather than defended ===

quest's six native-execution jobs ran on their PR, pre-tag, before the version was frozen. lore's
six-host `matching-host package qualification` matrix lives in release.yml, which is
workflow_dispatch-only, so it runs ON the tag. Same coverage, different failure cost: a failure on
lore's side is remedied by a NEW TAG, which is in the irreversible set that goes to this repo's own
user, and which also turns quest-web red because its check fetches external links live and cites
lore-cli. A gate with a more expensive failure mode, not a missing one. Not filed as a finding;
recorded here because "not a gap" was too flat an answer and theirs was better shaped.

What ran on the promoted SHA is ci.yml, whose `compile smoke (ubuntu)` is host-native compile only
on ubuntu x64 -- its own comment says so. "Green on main" is therefore NOT evidence about the six
platform packages and must not be reported as if it were.

AC 7 -- publish first, then qualify, per the user's ruling. opum-cli-e2e's pair qualification is a

=== A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE, AND THE POST-TAG LIST. 2026-09-15 ===

CORRECTING THE "PAIR-LEVEL FACT" I RECORDED EARLIER TODAY. That note said opum-cli-e2e's strict
error-envelope allow-list binds BOTH CLIs permanently, and concluded: "neither repo should treat the
missing metadata on its error envelopes as an oversight to fix in a later release: the fix turns
their checks red whenever it lands."

THAT CONCLUSION IS VOID. It was true about the harness's behavior and wrong about what the behavior
meant. opum-doc ratified an amendment (their PR #274; the spec's Adoption section names dev as the
stable reference, so it is live) making top-level envelope key sets OPEN to addition on BOTH the
success and error envelope, permitted without a breaking change, with only the identity category
`principal` occupies keeping a ratification bar. opum-cli-e2e accepted that their strict allow-list
is therefore a CONSUMER DEFECT rather than a constraint either CLI must design around, and filed
their TASK-66.

The correction is recorded rather than the note edited, because the reasoning that produced the
wrong conclusion is the part worth keeping: all three of us reasoned from a harness's behavior to a
contract's meaning. opum-doc's ruling names the rule that prevents it -- a harness ENFORCES a spec,
it is not the spec's SOURCE, so a harness/spec disagreement is a harness defect and never grounds
for reading the harness back into the spec. Two of the three constraints relayed to this repo as
facts turned out to be one repository's reading of a silence.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: lore added no top-level envelope key in 0.7.0 and data.backend (LCLI-499)
is nested inside `data`, so lore was never exposed on any reading. Nothing about the 0.7.0 CHANGELOG
or the release changes.

=== AC 4: THE CROSS-READ IS DONE, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN A BRANCH READ ===

AT THAT EXACT SHA rather than at a branch name -- a branch can move between two calls, a SHA cannot:

  gh api "repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/contents/package.json?ref=f21de3fb..."  -> 0.7.0
  git/matching-refs/tags                                                  -> v0.6.0/1/2 only
  npm view @opum-ai/quest version                                         -> 0.6.2
  npm view @opum-ai/quest@0.7.0                                           -> E404

tags v0.6.0/1/2, nothing published. THE PAIR IS MATCHED AT 0.7.0 AND NEITHER IS TAGGED.

Note that the lockstep is a fact about VERSIONS, not SHAs. A tracker-only commit moves a SHA without
touching the lockstep, so a moved SHA after this point does not invalidate the pairing -- re-read the
version, not the commit.

=== A PEER CLAIM THAT WAS WRONG, AND HOW IT WAS CAUGHT ===

quest-cli stated that lore's target.body finding was "squarely addressed by the spec -- the
breaking-change list names it explicitly", and offered that as the asymmetry making it safe for lore
to agree to tag-and-publish in parallel. Reading the spec directly showed it is not: the clause says
"renaming, removing, or repurposing an existing ENVELOPE field (including schemaVersion, kind, data,
or the reserved principal slot's name/position)", and section 2 defines the envelope as exactly that
top-level wrapper with `data` opaque. target.body is data.target.body, a payload field. The permitted
list says "adding fields to `data`" and never addresses REMOVING from data.

So both findings sit outside both enumerated lists. quest-cli verified the blob themselves and
withdrew the claim. The conclusion (tag and publish as planned) survived on a replaced premise:
neither is breaking under the spec's own definition, both are documented where a consumer reads them,
and holding the pair on an unaddressed question costs more than the ambiguity.

RECORDED AS METHOD, NOT AS SCOREKEEPING: the claim would have been convenient to accept, because it
made lore's position the stronger one. Checking a peer's claim matters most exactly when it favours
you.

=== THE POST-TAG LIST, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE A LIST THAT LIVES IN MESSAGES IS NOT A LIST ===

This is the defect this task was created to fix, so these go here rather than staying in message
traffic with an orchestrator that is being recycled.

1. RECONCILE cli-contract 7.1 WITH THE RATIFIED WORDING. lore's section 7.1 says "renaming, removing,
   or repurposing an existing FIELD" where opum-doc's spec says "an existing ENVELOPE field", and the
   spec states it mirrors lore's section 7 discipline. They do not match; lore's local text is

Post-tag item 3 on this task described the init/wizard flake as three test-level 10000ms timeouts on

MAIN CI ON THE PROMOTED TIP 7d0e3b2b CAME BACK **CANCELLED**, NOT GREEN. The cause was
`lint / typecheck / test (macos-latest)` hanging for the job's FULL `timeout-minutes: 20` and being

at 2m58s, 3m07s and 3m05s on the three immediately preceding main runs. The re-run took 3m15s and
passed, so main CI is green on 7d0e3b2b now.

THIS WAS NOT A SUPERSEDED RUN AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. ci.yml's concurrency group is
`${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}` with
`cancel-in-progress` true ONLY for pull_request events, so a push run's group key is its own unique
run_id and can never be auto-cancelled. No newer main run existed. The job had a startedAt, so it was
running rather than queued. It hung.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE RELEASE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF RECORDING IT HERE RATHER THAN ON A BACKLOG
ITEM: a cancelled run reports as neither success nor failure, and `gh run list` shows
`completed/cancelled`. A session checking "is main green" with a loose predicate reads that as
not-failed and moves on. The tag is cut from main, and release.yml's six-host native matrix is far
longer than this job -- if a 3-minute job can hang for 20, a 60-minute-timeout package qualification
can hang too, and a failure THERE is remedied by a new tag, which is in the irreversible set.

SO THE HANDOFF INSTRUCTION IS: BEFORE THE TAG, CONFIRM main CI IS `success` EXPLICITLY -- not
"not failed". `gh run list --branch main --limit 1 --json conclusion` must read exactly "success".
Cancelled is a third state and it is the one that looks like nothing happened.
